_comment: Corpus for compare-sims.mjs. Every skill and course here is present in BOTH engines'
data/ with a semantically identical definition, so a failure points at the engine, not
at our JP data being stale. compare-sims re-verifies this at runtime and tags any case
whose data has since drifted apart.
Chosen to span the sample-policy space: immediate/static regions, the *_random
policies (corner, phase, final corner), accumulatetime distributions, and the
debuff path that gain.ts splits into a separate solver.

cases._why: No CLI skill: both solvers run the same build. Expectation is 0 gain in both engines; isolates pure RNG/integration drift.
100271 Let's Anabolic! — phase>=2&corner!=0. Fires at 0m delay when phase 2 opens mid-corner; the premium accel bucket.
100041 Red Flame Gear — is_finalcorner==1. Separate bucket from phase2&corner; Tokyo 2400 is where finalCorner.start ~= phase2 start.
100701 Seirios — narrow remain_distance window, exercises tight region intersection.
100071 Unsinkable Ship, Anchored! — distance_rate band, plain TargetSpeed with no dynamic gate. Fires mid-race, so it tests speed carryover into phase 2.
100031 Ultimate Teio Step — is_last_straight==1, a large TargetSpeed deep in the spurt.
110391 Invigorating Strength — slope==0@slope==2. The '@' makes it the only case exercising buildSkillData's alternative-selection fallback.
100011 Shooting Star — type 22 CurrentSpeedWithNaturalDeceleration + type 31 Accel in one skill.
200331 Archline Professor — all_corner_random, RandomPolicy sampled across every corner.
210011 Aoharu Burning Speed — phase_random. Also one of the scenario skills carrying the x1.2 modifier patch.
200371 Gust of Wind — straight_random, accel + velocity together on a StraightRandomPolicy.
203331 Thorough Preparation — phase_firsthalf_random, gated to sasi; samples only the first half of a phase.
202301 Leisurely Dust Bath — ground_type==2 & accumulatetime, the distribution-sampled policy. Needs a dirt course to activate at all.

100451 Purity of Heart — recovery (type 9). gain.ts runs NoopHpPolicy, so this is expected to measure exactly 0 in both engines. Kept as a control: if it ever stops reading 0, one engine started simulating HP here.
100251 Chasing After You — mixed buff + negative modifier; gain.ts splits the negative effects onto the *baseline* solver.
Stacked kit: overlapping durations and multiple concurrent modifiers are where small integration differences compound.
Same case as the phase2-corner baseline but on heavy ground, exercising the speed/power ground modifiers.
Sprint: phases are compressed, so region intersection is much tighter.
